title: Senate language on historical exotic technology antecedents (Lockheed's basement)

tellings.quote: if you read the language in, you know, it's come out of the the Senate, you know, in order to mitigate the possibility of of foreign technology surprise, the US government must broaden awareness of quote historical exotic technology anticedants previously provided by the federal government for research and development purposes.

plain: Language that came out of the US Senate in 2023 and 2024, in its laws on UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena, the government's current word for UFOs), hints that the government once handed strange technology to private companies for research. That is how the national security analyst Matthew Pines reads it to Michels. He quotes it: to avoid being surprised by foreign technology, the government "must broaden awareness of historical exotic technology antecedents previously provided by the federal government for research and development purposes." Pines takes this to point at material held by defence contractors such as Lockheed. The wording does say exotic technology was given out for research, but what it was, where it came from and who got it, it does not say.
